repository.name: @webex/plugin-presence
repository.purpose: Public TypeScript plugin registered as webex.presence for the presence service (catalog name apheleia). get() reads one user's composed presence; list() reads many through a Batcher that folds lookups into POST compositions; subscribe() POSTs subscriptions in batches of 50 and unsubscribe() sends subscriptionTtl 0; setStatus() POSTs events for the device user, without a label for dnd; enable(), disable(), and isEnabled() set and read the user-presence-enabled toggle through the feature plugin. Registration adds an inbound transform that copies body.eventType to body.status. An optional PresenceWorker, started by initializeWorker() or config.presence.initializeWorker, counts enqueue/dequeue watchers, fetches stale presence after a 300 ms debounce, subscribes users watched for a minute, renews watched subscriptions, listens to the Mercury event apheleia.subscription_update, expires update times after 10 minutes, and reports every change as an 'updated' event with a subscription, presence, or delete envelope. src/interface.ts types the surface; build emits declarations to dist/types. It stores nothing.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/plugin-presence package entry
public_interfaces.audience: applications that install the package from npm beside @webex/webex-core
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package imports the device plugin, then registers Presence as public plugin 'presence' with config.presence defaults {batcherWait: 50, batcherMaxCalls: 50, batcherMaxWait: 150} and the inbound transform normalizeSingleStatusResponse, which copies body.eventType to body.status on any response with body.eventType and body.subject; the first registration of the name wins. The default export is the only export; no workspace package imports this package.

public_interfaces.name: webex.presence methods and events
public_interfaces.notes: Requests go to the apheleia service; list batches lookups into POST compositions; subscribe sends at most 50 subjects per request; setStatus leaves out label for dnd; unsubscribe resolves the whole response. enable, disable, and isEnabled need the host to register the feature plugin. The worker emits 'updated' with {type: 'subscription' | 'presence' | 'delete', payload}.

public_interfaces.name: TypeScript declarations
public_interfaces.notes: package.json types points to dist/types/index.d.ts, which only build (tsc) writes. It declares the default Presence as IPresence. IPresence omits initializeWorker and types unsubscribe as {responses: any}; the entry re-exports no type. typedoc (build:docs) renders src/interface.ts.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not store presence objects in the worker.
negative_guidance.why: The client owns presence data and receives it through 'updated' envelopes.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not send more than 50 subjects in one subscribe request.
negative_guidance.why: The code comment limits batches to 50 ids per request.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not widen the inbound transform predicate.
negative_guidance.why: It runs on every inbound SDK response, not only presence responses.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not start another interval or Mercury listener without a way to stop it.
negative_guidance.why: Nothing removes the existing ones; each start duplicates work and events.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not log presence data, statuses, or user ids.
negative_guidance.why: They are other users' personal data; the package has no log line today.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md as a usage reference.
negative_guidance.why: Its Usage block names a placeholder member; see docs/adr/0001-retain-product-readme.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: No coverage script or threshold exists.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not change a method signature without changing src/interface.ts.
negative_guidance.why: The published declarations come from it, and they already omit initializeWorker.

high.expectation: Source and a running unit case agree, as for the argument checks, subscribe batching, the dnd label rule, initializeWorker, and the worker map rules.

medium.expectation: Only source evidence, or a skipped integration case, exists, as for registration, the transform, the feature toggle, the batcher, and the Mercury update. Pin current behavior with a running unit case before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source, tests, nor a dependency's spec or code settles the question. Stop and report the gap.
